description.narrative: CDKN works globally and across the three regions of Africa, Asia and Latin America. Focal countries are Colombia, Ecuador and Peru in Latin America.

The CDKN programme: Accelerating inclusive climate action is a five-year project that builds on the previous two phases of CDKN. Building on the success of this second phase, funding for a third phase – Accelerating inclusive climate action – is being provided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands and IDRC through the Step Change Initiative, which aims to accelerate equitable and inclusive LLA. This new phase of CDKN focusses on accelerating equitable, financed and ecosystem-based action on climate change that is locally-led and supports the voice and climate leadership of marginalised groups. It has three objectives:1. Gender equity and social inclusion (GESI): Supporting the integration of GESI in policies and practice that achieve climate-resilient development.2. Finance for resilience: Improving access to appropriate and equitable finance that enables locally-led solutions.3. Ecosystem-based adaptation (EbA) approaches: Strengthening the implementation of equitable and locally-appropriate EbA to build the resilience of climate-affected communities and settlements.

The Climate and Development Knowledge Network (CDKN) is a partnership of Southern leaders, implementing a global programme that drives climate action across public, civil society and private sectors in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Building on 14 years of experience working in the global South, CDKN is mobilising knowledge, capacity and leadership through diverse knowledge co-production processes to improve the well-being and resilience of the most climate-affected people, through transformative climate action. CDKN was launched in 2010 to advance climate-resilient development in the global South. It was funded by the United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth and Development office - FCDO, which at the time was named the Department of International Development (DFID). The programme was led by the London office of PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) with ODI, and regional partners in Latin America: Fundación Futuro Latinoamericano (FFLA), Asia: LEAD Pakistan, and Africa: SouthSouthNorth (SSN) who were implementing a largely technical assistance, research commissioning and knowledge management programme. A second phase of CDKN: Knowledge Accelerator was funded by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands (MOFA) and Canada’s International Development Research Centre (IDRC). It was distinct from the first phase in a few ways. The leadership of the programme moved from the global North to the global South, with SouthSouthNorth taking over leadership of the programme as well as Africa, and the global region. Furthermore, one new implementation partner joined the alliance of SSN, FFLA, and ODI, namely ICLEI South Asia. The programme also changed in nature, from focussing on a combination of technical assistance, research and knowledge-sharing services to focussing exclusively on our knowledge programme and moving knowledge into increased action on climate change, using a knowledge brokering approach.

title.narrative: CDKN technical report year 2 2024 ( 6 July 2023 to 5 July 2024)

description.narrative: Now in year 2, the Climate and Development Knowledge Network (CDKN) can report significant progress in its third phase: Accelerating inclusive climate action. To date, it has produced 37 knowledge products, engaged 3,757 key actors and climate knowledge brokers (approx 56% women) in its knowledge sharing and capacity strengthening activities, secured 40 new partnerships and kicked off 11 Knowledge-to-Action (K2A) projects supporting locally-led adaptation (LLA) in eight countries in Africa and Latin America. 515 organisations have been involved in CDKN’s capacity strengthening work. CDKN has already overshot the mid-term target for capacity strengthening, knowledge sharing and partnership activities. CDKN is now supporting adaptation and resilience building in nine African countries that span both Anglophone and Francophone regions: Benin, Cameroon, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Mozambique, Namibia, Senegal and South Sudan. Across Africa, Asia, Latin America and at global levels, the respective teams have established or further strengthened relationships with target key actors, including with a range of local and grassroots organisations in Africa and Latin America in supporting LLA, a number of municipalities in South Asia, water funds in Latin America, national governments in Namibia and Ethiopia, county governments in Kenya, young climate leaders and youth groups in Ghana and Ethiopia, and multiple UN agencies and knowledge networks at international levels. In the reporting period, CDKN also contracted ENDA Energie in Senegal to lead CDKN’s work in that country, CDKN’s first partnership within the Francophone region.
